scope: Smallest coherent source-level correction proposals for F01 and required delayed recovery.

findings.current_cause: Home reconcileExpiry treats refresh expiry as session expiry even while access remains valid. Timeout then schedules logout.
findings.proposal: Keep the existing refresh timer. On refresh-only expiry, replace the refresh credential through the valid access token. Show Timeout only when access expires.
required_checks: Preserve active access at initial refresh expiry.
Acquire a genuinely usable replacement refresh credential.
Do not send extend or relogin solely because the refresh deadline fired.
Future idle recovery uses the replacement credential.
limits: This is a proposal, not a passing execution.
Existing fixtures that return the same expired refresh token must not be treated as replacement verification.
findings.backend_contract: The refresh acquisition endpoint validates the access JWT, issuer, and server session. It generates a refresh credential without requiring the previous refresh token.

findings.current_cause: Timeout mount executes once. With no refresh credential, it starts logout immediately and disables both buttons. Late credentials cannot cancel that decision.
findings.proposal: Peek the current-session acquisition already in flight. Wait for its settlement, then react to context refresh changes. Never start acquisition after access expiry. Return relogin promise, keep the dialog during pending/error, and reset loading.

required_shared_helper.name: getPendingRefreshToken
required_shared_helper.ownership: Return only an un-aborted request matching the current session epoch. This comes from the paired F03 proposal.
required_shared_helper.settlement: Reject acquisition failures. The Timeout waiter handles both settlement branches without reading context imperatively.

required_checks: No logout begins while current-session acquisition is pending.
Late usable refresh enables Extend without an automatic relogin.
Pending relogin leaves the dialog open until actual successful completion.
Missing, malformed, or already-expired access response headers reject relogin completion and leave the dialog open.
Current-session transient rejection resets loading and permits retry while refresh remains usable.
No refresh and no pending request preserves existing logout fallback.
Explicit Logout cancels or invalidates pending session work.
Refresh expiry during relogin does not start a competing popup logout timer.
Request timeout or rejected acquisition settles waiting without an unhandled rejection.
limits: No new grace interval is proposed. The existing Axios request timeout is 60000 milliseconds.
Preserve the existing two-second pre-expiry logout margin. Its policy authority remains unresolved; this proposal does not establish a new timeout rule.
The returned relogin promise validates the access response header and future expiry. The current-session response interceptor must install that credential before completion.

A current-request TOKEN_INVALID_EXPIRED error still clears storage in the interceptor. Revoked or expired credential handling needs a fail-closed distinction from retryable transport/provider failure.
The snippets require the session-epoch response guard from the F03 design. Old-session success/error responses must not update current state.
The effect reads context after render. It avoids testing getHooksBase().store directly inside promise settlement, before React applies response dispatches.

limitations: Automated checks do not check the complete approved dictionary or grammar rules.
JSON parse and required proposal-field validation passed. No prose dictionary or grammar check ran.
